title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 SERVFAIL Response Architecture
purpose: Define the DoQ adapter behavior for preserving handler-provided SERVFAIL DNS responses without transport remapping.
design_summary: The DoQ server writes the handler-provided DNS response payload back to the peer on the same bidirectional stream. The adapter does not inspect or rewrite DNS response codes, so a handler that returns a SERVFAIL payload delivers that SERVFAIL response to the client unchanged.
data_and_state_considerations: No new adapter state is needed for SERVFAIL pass-through. The response remains an opaque DNS payload at the DoQ layer, subject only to the existing two-octet length prefix and zero-message-ID client checks.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The response must still carry a zero DNS Message ID to satisfy DoQ framing expectations.
The adapter does not derive SERVFAIL from exceptions; it only preserves the handler-provided response payload.
risks: This slice does not add a dedicated resolver implementation or DNS message builder.
The proof uses a focused loopback payload check rather than a resolver-backed end-to-end scenario.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: DNS resolver policy that decides when to emit SERVFAIL remains above the transport adapter. The DoQ layer only preserves the bytes supplied by the handler.
